memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So all the Israelites twenty years old or more, those able to serve in Israel's army, were counted according to their families. The total number was 603,550. - Num 1:45-46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The final number is staggering — over six hundred thousand men able to serve, not even counting women and children. This once-enslaved people had become a vast nation. What God had promised to Abraham long ago was now visible before their eyes.

Behind this great number stands a greater truth: God is faithful across generations. The people counted here were the grandchildren and great-grandchildren of those who had suffered as slaves in Egypt. Their ancestors may have wondered whether God had forgotten them. But He had not. In His time, He multiplied and delivered them.

We must not read this as a promise that God will make us all rich or numerous. That would twist the passage. The point is not material prosperity but the unchanging faithfulness of God. He keeps His word — always.

This huge number also reminds us of our smallness before God and His power to work on a scale we cannot imagine. The One who led six hundred thousand through the wilderness is more than able to guide your one life through your own uncertain seasons.

If God was faithful to a whole nation over centuries, He will be faithful to you today. Rest in the God who never forgets and never fails.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where do you need to remember God's faithfulness right now?
- Do you ever feel God has forgotten you? What does this passage say?
- How can you rest in God's power over your circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Almighty God, You are faithful beyond my understanding. Help me to trust that You have not forgotten me, and that You are working even when I cannot see it. Amen.
